_comment: Every `clipboard` reply this phone claims to understand, asserted from
BOTH ends. `Agentd.readClipboard` parses this file in
AgentdClipboardReplyTest; apexd/apex-agent-core/tests/
android_clipboard_wire.rs deserializes the same entries into
Response::Clipboard and round-trips them. Neither half alone is worth
much: a Kotlin test reading a string a Kotlin author wrote proves the
two agree with each other, not that the daemon sends it.
The request direction already had this treatment (requests.json). This
is the reply direction, which had none -- `readClipboard` was written
and shipped with no test on either side.
`empty` is the case that matters most and the easiest to get wrong. An
empty string is a REAL answer meaning the machine's clipboard is empty,
not a failure and not a missing field. Response::Clipboard's own
documentation says so. A client that reported it as an error would send
somebody hunting for a permission to grant when the machine simply had
nothing on it, and a client that reported it as nothing at all would
read as a button that does not work.
`multiline` carries the newline and the quote that NDJSON framing cares
about, because a clipboard holds whatever was last copied and that is
routinely a stack trace. It is the same text protocol.rs uses in its own
round-trip case, copied from there rather than invented here.
